title: docs: correct silence-token scope; note human-turn fallback reply
claim: Silence-token docs should note the human-turn fallback reply and narrow the scope away from group chats.

evidence.source: Main's messaging/index.md:157 already documents it: 'On a message from a person, a bare silence token is replaced by a short notice ... a message the platform adapter reports as not addressed to the bot [may stay silent]. Slack reports this for messages that open by @mentioning someone else and for unmentioned top-level messages ... in a free-response channel'. Added by 6c566fcd6d (fix(slack): thread follow-ups and reaction triggers keep the silence-marker fallback). Because Slack free-response group messages can still be silenced, the fork's removal of 'group chats' from the scope sentence would now be wrong.

notes: Residual nit only: the transcript example 'user: side-channel chatter' is valid for the Slack not-addressed case; not worth a change.
